events.content:
I confirmed the bottleneck: `app/page.tsx` waits on one blocking `getDashboardData()` call before rendering anything meaningful, so the PPR shell can’t stream early.  

Plan:
1. Refactor `app/page.tsx` into a static shell that renders immediately and wraps each data-heavy section in its own `Suspense` boundary.
2. Split server data fetching into section-level async server components so each part can stream independently instead of waiting on one aggregate fetch.
3. Add lightweight skeleton fallbacks matched to the final layout to improve perceived speed during partial pre-rendering.
4. Run a production build to verify the route still compiles and streams cleanly with the new structure.

I confirmed the bottleneck: `app/page.tsx` waits on one blocking `getDashboardData()` call before rendering anything meaningful, so the PPR shell can’t stream early.  

Plan:
1. Refactor `app/page.tsx` into a static shell that renders immediately and wraps each data-heavy section in its own `Suspense` boundary.
2. Split server data fetching into section-level async server components so each part can stream independently instead of waiting on one aggregate fetch.
3. Add lightweight skeleton fallbacks matched to the final layout to improve perceived speed during partial pre-rendering.
4. Run a production build to verify the route still compiles and streams cleanly with the new structure.

- Added lightweight, layout-matching fallback skeletons for each streamed section in [app/page.tsx:48](/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx#L48).
- Preloaded the shared dashboard request at shell render start (`void getDashboardData()`) in [app/page.tsx:65](/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx#L65).
